subject.title: feat(android): durable offline command outbox for chat sends

question: Should Android text-only offline commands ship as app-private Room rows with destructive schema-bump semantics after correctness fixes and real-device proof, or should the outbox wait for a stronger non-destructive privacy and upgrade design?
rationale: The PR persists user-authored commands before Gateway delivery and replays them later, so automation cannot choose the storage, privacy, retention, and upgrade-loss boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Fix, prove, then sign off
options.body: Keep the PR open, fix the delivery and lifecycle bugs, add redacted Android real-behavior proof, and require explicit maintainer acceptance of storage, retention, and migration behavior before merge.

options.title: Move outbox to non-destructive storage
options.body: Require a separate migrated or dedicated persistent store for queued commands before accepting durable offline sends.

options.title: Pause the feature stack
options.body: Close or hold this PR until the canonical offline command outbox issue has a broader mobile privacy and replay contract.

recommendation.title: Fix, prove, then sign off
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, fix the delivery and lifecycle bugs, add redacted Android real-behavior proof, and require explicit maintainer acceptance of storage, retention, and migration behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the active Android outbox/cache author and strongest current-history owner for the affected Android runtime path.
